content: A total of 12 writers with expertise in human–computer interaction (HCI) participated in the study (9 female, 3 male; ages 23–29). All had experience in English academic writing, and 7 had prior academic publication experience in the HCI field. Participants were intentionally recruited from the HCI domain, as they represent a population for whom reflective academic writing is a routine yet demanding practice and who possess the analytical skills required to critically interrogate interactive system behavior.
